NOVELTY STATEMENT
Standard practice delivers a MONITORING/INDICATION scheme using offline partial discharge or resistance-to-earth megger tests to track insulation degradation.
My same-class mechanism departure is a purely computational, firmware-based inference engine that calculates the Arrhenius insulation life rate in real-time using only the existing stator current and winding RTD, completely excluding physical degradation proxies (like PD or Megger) to predict thermal time-to-failure.
The failure-physics connection is that insulation thermal aging is driven exclusively by the thermal integral (temperature-time exposure); by precisely computing the actual peak winding temperature from stator current (I²R heating proxy) and RTD, the mechanism directly quantifies the physical driver of dielectric breakdown without needing invasive sensors.

PHYSICS CHECK
Governing physical relation: The rate of insulation aging is governed by the Arrhenius law for chemical degradation, where the life rate $L$ is proportional to $e^{(E_a/RT)}$. For Class F insulation, the standard thermal life model uses a base temperature of 155°C for a 40,000-hour (approx. 4.6 years) life. The Arrhenius factor for 10K°C temperature rise is 2 (the "rule of 10" for Class F).
Magnitude verification: At 400 V, stator current $I$ is directly proportional to torque and thermal heating ($P_{heat} \propto I^2 R$). By integrating the real-time RTD temperature $T_{winding}(t)$ and adjusting for current density $\Delta T \propto I^2$, the system computes the instantaneous temperature $T_{actual}$. The daily life consumption is calculated as $10^{((T_{actual}-155)/10)}$. If the 10-day moving average of $T_{actual}$ exceeds 165°C, the daily life consumption is $10^1 = 10$ days of life. A 90-day warning is triggered when the remaining unaged life equals 90 days.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
MECHANISM CLASS: Firmware-Based Thermal-Life Accumulator
(a) Existing PLC/Controller Firmware Update: No new hardware. (b) Access existing stator current telemetry stream. (c) Access existing winding RTD telemetry stream. (d) Access existing run-hours counter.
DERIVED (Stated Spec): Class F insulation base life of 155°C and 10°C Arrhenius doubling rule.
DERIVED (Stated Data): Stator current, winding RTD, and run-hours are explicitly stated in the user constraints as existing data.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
Installability: Zero new sensors or cables. Operability: Pure background process, no operator intervention required for data collection. Maintenance: No calibration of physical sensors (unlike megger or PD sensors). Cost: Firmware license only (approx. $500 - $2,000) versus $5,000 - $15,000 for megger/PD equipment.
UNPRICED_OPERATIONAL_LOSS: 0 hours of downtime for installation. 0 operational loss because it runs on existing telemetry.

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: Run the motor at a controlled overload (e.g., 110% rated current) until the RTD reaches 175��C.
Instruments: Existing RTD and current logger.
Pass/Fail Thresholds: The algorithm must calculate that 175°C consumes 100 days of life per day of operation.
Duration: 24 hours of continuous operation at 175°C.
Kill Criterion: If the algorithm calculates 9 days of life consumption instead of 100, the Arrhenius coefficient is wrong and the 90-day warning will fail.

CONSTRAINT BIND
Primary Stated Indicator: Winding Temperature (RTD). It is the direct physical proxy for the thermal integral that drives insulation aging. Stator current supplements it by providing the $I^2R$ correction factor for the RTD location bias.
Permitted-Set Clause: The constraint explicitly states "use only the existing stator current, winding RTD and run-hours; no new sensors". No physical measures, only parameter/procedure (computational) measures are used.
Direction-of-Effect: Driving variable = Winding Temperature. The mechanism does NOT move the temperature; it measures the temperature and its integral to predict the time-to-failure. It moves the *awareness* of the failure driver UP by 90 days, reducing the risk of undetected insulation breakdown.
Input-Availability: Stator current (existing), RTD (existing), run-hours (existing). All are legally and physically obtainable.
